subject: gk
question: The Indian government launched the ‘Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan’ (‘GKRA’) on 20th June 2020 to provide work for how many days?
solution:
The correct answer is __**125 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The 'Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan' (GKRA) was launched by the Indian government on 20th June 2020.

• The campaign aims to provide livelihood opportunities to migrant workers who returned to their home states due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

• The program is designed to offer 125 days of employment to these workers, thus ensuring they have a source of income during this period.

• It is a rural public works campaign that includes various projects like plantation, rural housing, rural connectivity, and more, which help in the development of rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA)**

• It is an initiative by the Government of India to address the economic distress faced by migrant workers due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

• The scheme was launched in 116 districts across 6 states, which include Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, and Odisha.

• It involves the coordination of 12 different ministries including Rural Development, Panchayati Raj, Road Transport and Highways, Mines, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Environment, Railways, Petroleum and Natural Gas, and more.

• The GKRA aims to create public infrastructure and enhance livelihood opportunities in rural areas.

• **COVID-19 Pandemic**

• The COVID-19 pandemic is an ongoing global pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2).

• It was first identified in December 2019 in Wuhan, Hubei, China.

• The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 30 January 2020, and a pandemic on 11 March 2020.

• The pandemic has led to global social and economic disruption, including the largest global recession since the Great Depression.
